about.title: Brea Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision on roads like SR-57 Southbound, Imperial Highway, or Lambert Road changes everything, and the paperwork that follows can feel impossible to face while grieving. Orange County recorded 3 traffic deaths in Brea in the most recent final crash year, alongside 211 injury collisions, numbers that represent real families going through what yours may be facing now. California law gives close family members, and in some cases other dependents, the right to pursue a wrongful death claim, but that right comes with a strict two-year deadline from the date of death. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect grieving families in Brea with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the crash, explain what compensation may be available, and handle communication with insurers so you can focus on your family. There's no cost to get connected, and no fee unless the attorney recovers on your behalf.

whyChoose.title: Why Brea Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to spouses, domestic partners, and children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain situations. An attorney can help clarify where your family stands before decisions are made under pressure.

items.title: A Deadline That Doesn't Wait
items.desc: Wrongful death claims in California generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shortens significantly if a government entity was involved. Connecting early with an attorney helps protect your family's ability to pursue the claim.

items.title: Losses Beyond the Bills
items.desc: California law recognizes recoverable losses that go beyond funeral and burial costs, including lost financial support and the loss of a loved one's love, companionship, and guidance. An independent attorney can help make sure these losses aren't overlooked.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may be able to step in depending on the circumstances. An attorney can review your family's situation and explain where you stand.

items.question: Does the wrongful death claim replace any criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal charges the driver may face. The civil case focuses on compensation for your family, while the criminal case is handled independently by prosecutors. You can pursue the civil claim regardless of the criminal outcome.

items.question: Our loved one died in a crash near Imperial Highway in Brea involving a city vehicle. Does that change anything?
items.answer: Yes, claims involving a government entity, such as a city-owned vehicle, generally carry a much shorter filing deadline than the standard two years. It's important to speak with an attorney as soon as possible so any required notice isn't missed. Waiting even a few weeks can affect your options.
